scope.summary: Implement FBX delivery via the Blender-bridge ONLY per Section 13.26 and the file-format strategy verdict: reuse the MT-419 bridge pattern (glTF -> headless Blender -> FBX) for the body skeletal lane including blendshapes; a native FBX writer is PROHIBITED and the prohibition is guard-tested.
acceptance_criteria: FBX output is produced exclusively by driving headless Blender over the bridge (import the glTF core export, apply profile transforms, export FBX with blendshapes and skeleton); the bridge script is versioned in-repo.

A guard test proves the prohibition: no FBX-writing code path exists in Rust (no fbx writer dependency in Cargo.lock for handshake_core/tailor-solver; grep-guard on symbol names), matching the spec-level native-FBX-write prohibition.

Bridge failures (Blender missing, script error, version mismatch) surface as typed errors with the Blender stderr captured in the receipt; the lane records a SKIPPED-with-reason result in CI environments without Blender.
Bridged FBX carries cm units and the profile's axis contract; blendshape names survive the trip (verified by re-importing the FBX in Blender and diffing shape-key names).
scope.risk_if_missed: Either the legacy UE/DCC FBX lane is missing entirely, or someone reinvents a native FBX writer against the explicit spec prohibition and ships a licensing/compatibility time bomb.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit publishing and DCC interchange

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT must wire the shared internal_diagnostics API for its native, job, device, solver-run, or DCC failure modes with bounded structured evidence.
Long-running, native, or external-process work must register bounded progress and child/process identity with the shared Palmistry watcher; Tailor must not fork a watcher.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.
